findings.title: Sender/user validation is bypassed when Integration record doesn't exist yet (webhook race)
findings.body: In GitHubInstallation.dispatch, when Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id) raises DoesNotExist, the code immediately returns pipeline.next_step() (line 482), completely skipping the newly added 'github_authenticated_user' vs 'sender.login' check that appears later (lines 500-505). Since the Integration row is normally created asynchronously by GitHub's webhook, there's a race window where the webhook hasn't been processed yet when the user's browser redirect reaches this view. In that window, the entire point of this PR (preventing a mismatch between the OAuth-authenticated GitHub user and the user who actually installed the app) is bypassed, allowing an attacker to complete installation under a different GitHub identity than the one that performed the OAuth authorize step.

findings.title: KeyError if integration.metadata lacks 'sender' key
findings.body: The check `integration.metadata['sender']['login']` assumes 'sender' is always present in metadata. However, build_integration() only sets metadata['sender'] conditionally (`if state.get('sender')`), so there are legitimate code paths where an Integration can exist without a 'sender' key in its metadata. If that happens, this line raises a KeyError, producing an unhandled 500 error instead of the intended graceful 'invalid installation request' error page.

findings.title: safe_urlopen call for OAuth token exchange is not wrapped in error handling
findings.body: `req = safe_urlopen(url=ghip.get_oauth_access_token_url(), data=data)` can raise an exception (e.g. ApiError, network failure) but only the subsequent safe_urlread/parse_qsl call is wrapped in try/except (lines 425-429). Any failure from safe_urlopen itself (GitHub API down, network error, etc.) will propagate as an unhandled exception, resulting in a 500 error for the user instead of the intended friendly 'invalid installation request' error page.

findings.title: test_installation_not_found no longer exercises the 'installation not found' code path
findings.body: The rewritten test now sends a mismatched `state` value ("ddd023d87a913d5226e2a882c4c4cc05") that does not match the pipeline signature used elsewhere in the suite ("9cae5e88803f35ed7970fc131e6e65d3"). As a result, the request is rejected early by the new state-check in OAuthLoginView.dispatch, before ever reaching build_integration()/get_installation_info(), which is where the 404-handling logic ('The GitHub installation could not be found.') lives. The assertion was changed to match the generic 'Invalid installation request.' message, so the original 404 'installation not found' behavior added in build_integration is no longer covered by any test, while the test name/intent remains misleading.

findings.title: New OAuth failure branches lack test coverage
findings.body: The new OAuthLoginView introduces several failure branches: 'access_token' missing from the token exchange response (line 431-432), and 'login' missing from get_user_info's response (lines 435-436). None of these branches are exercised by the added tests, so regressions in this new security-critical logic (e.g. incorrectly treating a failed token exchange as success) would not be caught.

findings.title: Authorize URL built via string interpolation instead of proper URL encoding
findings.body: The GitHub OAuth authorize URL is built with f-string interpolation (`f"{...}?client_id={github_client_id}&state={state}&redirect_uri={redirect_uri}"`) rather than urlencode(). The redirect_uri value itself contains characters ('://') that are not percent-encoded as a query value, and github_client_id/state are also inserted unescaped. If any of these values ever contain reserved query characters, the resulting URL could be mis-parsed by GitHub, breaking the install flow silently.
